meta.scenario: progressive house 32-bar long blend — same key, patient pad layering, bass swap at midpoint of 32-bar window, atmospheric handoff
meta.source: Sasha and John Digweed - Northern Exposure 2 (1997)

transition_arc: Both tracks share the same key (10B, E major). Progressive house demands patience: the 32-bar outro of T1 and the 32-bar intro of T2 are designed to mirror each other — T1 strips elements every 8 bars back toward percussion, T2 adds them every 8 bars toward the groove. The two arcs run simultaneously for 32 bars, producing a continuous-composition effect. Bass swap fires at bar 16 of the 32-bar window (bar 96 in this example) — the midpoint — when both tracks are at equal gain and the harmonic hand-off sounds most natural. The 4 BPM gap is imperceptible at progressive house tempos over a 32-bar blend because BPM changes accumulate to only ~1/8 note offset per 16 bars.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 0: full progressive groove, pad+bass+kick, RMS 0.50
T1 bar 72: 8 bars before T2 fade_in at bar 80. Outro beginning, drums=0.38, harmonic=0.30, rms=0.35
annotated_actions.why: Bass pre-cut 8 bars before T2 enters. Same key (10B→10B) means harmonic content could coexist; bass still cannot. low=0.0 (not 0.5) because even same-key bass overlap accumulates over 32 bars — the very long blend window makes even a brief 2-bar bass overlap audible as 'something was wrong for a moment.'
Kill T2 bass at fade start — prevents dual basslines during blend. EQ is persistent; will be restored at bass_swap point.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 80: outro, stripping toward percussion — drums=0.28, harmonic=0.20, rms=0.25
annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 8: sparse atmospheric intro, hi-hats + pads, no bass yet, drums=0.20, harmonic=0.15
annotated_actions.why: 32-bar long blend window — the signature of progressive house. other:0.7 is safe and correct: same key (10B=10B) means T2's pad/chord content is harmonically identical to T1's — layering them at 0.7 creates the 'two compositions merging' effect that defines this genre. drums:0.6 (not 0.8) — T2's intro percussion is introduced at moderate level to avoid a sudden rhythmic doubling on top of T1's still-present groove. from_bar=8 skips T2's 8 near-silent opening bars. stems={drums:0.8, bass:0.0, other:0.6} — T2 enters with 80% drums, no bass (held for bass_swap), 60% atmosphere.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 96: midpoint of 32-bar window, drums=0.18, harmonic=0.10, rms=0.18 — approaching sparse percussion tail
annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 24 (from_bar=8, 16 bars elapsed): bass entering, groove establishing at 124 BPM
annotated_actions.why: Midpoint of the 32-bar window (80 + 16 = 96). At this point both tracks are at equal gain (~50% each). T1's harmonic content is nearly gone (mostly percussion at this point in its outro). T2's groove is half-established. The bass swap at equal-gain crossover is the optimal balance: T2's bass arriving simultaneously with T1's bass departing sounds like a single continuous bass line changing character, not a swap.
Restore T2 bass at bass_swap point — T1 bass is now HPF-cut, T2 bass can come in.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 80: outro beginning, stripping elements every 8 bars
annotated_actions.why: Simultaneous with T2 fade_in. 32-bar fade_out mirrors T2's 32-bar fade_in. The symmetric duration is what creates the continuous-composition effect: T1 loses one element every 8 bars as T2 gains one. At bar 96 (midpoint) both are equal. At bar 112, T1 is gone and T2 is full.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 40 at 124 BPM: full progressive groove, pad+bass+kick, RMS 0.52
annotated_actions.why: T2 full groove arrives as T1 reaches zero. 32 bars of patient layering complete. from_bar = fade_in.from_bar(8) + fade_in.duration_bars(32) = 40. The audience experiences a single unbroken 32-bar arc from T1's world into T2's world — the genre's defining transition style.
